podcast.body: In 1994, Aphex Twin, operating under aliases such as Castig Windu, was developing material for a potential album and proceeded to press approximately 5,000 vinyl copies as a test. Ultimately, he decided against a formal release, and the project was abandoned. Years later, after the record label where he had worked changed locations, one of these vinyls was acquired by an individual through unstated means (implied theft from the "único que había en la discográfica"). This unique copy surfaced for sale on Discogs in January 2014, advertised as the "only existing copy" of his unreleased work, sparking significant collector interest. "Lo curioso es que 1994, 20 años atrás Apex Twin estaba trabajando en material y hizo una prueba para convertir eso en un álbum. Llego a trabajar a juntar muchos materiales, algunas bases, muchas cosas y lo llegó a prensar en 5.000."

podcast.body: The unreleased Castig Windu album contained a variety of tracks. Some of these songs had previously appeared in various Aphex Twin compilations throughout the 1990s, surprising those who acquired the album. A significant portion consisted of practically unfinished songs or tracks in a "precarious" state, along with numerous rhythmic bases and conceptual ideas intended for future albums. Aphex Twin had often used material from these vinyls, particularly other samples he kept, in his live DJ sets ("pinchadas") over the years, with many of these performances existing as bootlegs. "Las que ya habían sido editadas nos llevamos la sorpresa porque habían sido editadas en distintos recobulatorios de Apex Twin durante los 90. Muchas de ellas son canciones prácticamente no terminadas o en un estado un tanto precario y luego hay muchos sonidos de bases rítmicas y de ideas que iban a ser discos."
